content: Section 5 of the American Diabetes Association (ADA) guidelines has been revised to emphasize patient-centered approaches to promoting positive health behaviors. Point 4: The section has been expanded to incorporate a broader integration of cultural sensitivity in the delivery of patient care, ensuring that care is tailored to the diverse cultural backgrounds of individuals. Point 23: New guidance has been added advising individuals who do not consume alcohol to refrain from starting alcohol consumption for perceived health benefits. Point 31: The section on physical activity has been updated to include a clear definition of sedentary behavior and to address all types of diabetes. Additionally, it now includes discussions on the benefits of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) for individuals with diabetes. Point 33: The smoking cessation section has been updated to include considerations for cannabis use. Healthcare providers are now advised to routinely inquire about both tobacco and cannabis use during diabetes care and to provide appropriate referrals for cessation support. Point 36: The section now offers more detailed guidance on psychosocial screening protocols, with a focus on identifying and addressing diabetes-related mood concerns, stress, and quality-of-life issues. Point 39: Updates specify the recommended frequency for diabetes distress screening and emphasize the critical role of healthcare professionals in addressing diabetes-related stress as part of comprehensive care.
